producer_report.summary: Athena's own writers now keep boundary words out of the text that becomes a request or a record. Root cause: each writer copied model, record or file text into a request or record without checking it against the admission scan. On 2026-10-29 that left a steward proposal that approve-work could never admit. I added one shared check, `plain_boundary_text` in athena-context/src/briefs.rs, built on `boundary_words`, `boundary_fragments` and `boundary_scan`. It rewrites each boundary word to plain wording and each machine-path fragment to `[local path]`. The first word in the list becomes 'the person running Athena' and its plural 'the people running Athena'. Matching ignores case and keeps a leading capital. Text with no hit comes back unchanged. The result is scanned again, and a term that survives returns an Err naming it. Callers: (1) steward.rs: `StewardRequest::new` rewrites title, body and acceptance, which also covers the root-cause, spec, throughput and backfill requests. It refuses a file path with a hit, naming the term. `validate_item` rewrites the title and request and refuses a key with a hit. (2) hestia.rs: `root_cause_request_at` rewrites the cause, class and finished text, `try_error_review` rewrites the text before `self.queue`, and `mentions` compares the reworded cause. (3) introspect.rs: `apply_answer` rewrites the four prose fields and the new class name and description. An Err sets `record.failure`. The model's own words echoed into failure notes go through `withheld_if_unclean`. (4) work_decisions.rs: `approve_request` now returns `Result<String>` and rewrites the whole built request, because it copies in cited file, job and commit text. `approve_work` uses `?`. Tests: unit tests for the helper, one test per writer (steward proposal, a key and path refusal, Hestia error review, Hestia root-cause request, introspection writer), and an approve-work test. The approve-work test first shows the raw text is refused by `ask` with 'not admitted', then shows `approve_work` succeeds, the stored request is clean, `check_boundary_and_repo_files` passes and the decision names the job. CHANGELOG.md has a Fixed entry. Every test builds the boundary word from fragments.

open_issues: The plan asked for a helper unit test where a rewrite leaves a residue and returns Err. I could not build such an input without a test hook (the rewrite never recreates a hit), so that Err branch has no test. I added a test for the nearest real case instead: a word glued to a path fragment is cleared once the path is replaced.

A steward key that holds a listed word, such as 'lease-expiry', is refused and the item dropped. The key grammar leaves no safe rewrite, and a stored key is compared as written. The reason names the word, so the steward can retry with a plain key.
Work items and requests already written are not rewritten (out of scope). An old proposal is cleaned when approve-work builds its request.
mistakes: My first draft of the helper's unit tests had a test comment and fixture that did not match the behaviour: a word followed by '/' is already a whole-word hit. I replaced it before running the tests.
learnings: `StewardRequest::new` is the single builder for every steward-channel request (steward, root-cause, spec, throughput, backfill), so cleaning there covers all of them.

`queue` and `ask` both call `refuse_banned_input` (the boundary scan on the request text) before anything is committed. A refused request leaves no record, so the failed-admission step can be shown in a test without changing state.
A reader that declines (capability null with a decline_reason) still yields a committed proposal, so approve_work can be tested in athena-core with `test_support::make_athena` and no capability.

`plain_boundary_text` cannot easily return Err. Replacements are neutral, and rewriting a path fragment can uncover a word that was glued to it (for example a word followed straight by a path), but the word pass runs after the fragment pass and clears it. The Err branch is a defensive guard.
desires: Bash blocks `tail`, `grep` and pipes, and Read/Grep refuse paths outside the working directory. A long `cargo test` output that gets persisted elsewhere then cannot be read back, so I had to rerun the suite with `-q`.
